items.text: LPBS already exposes admin aggregation endpoints: GET /api/v1/metrics/summary (visitor/conversion analytics), GET /api/v1/admin/usage (usage records by period), GET /api/v1/admin/users (enriched user list with subscription + credits), GET /api/v1/admin/coupons/usage (coupon stats). However, there is NO revenue/MRR endpoint — subscription-to-amount mapping requires joining subscriptions.price_id against the in-memory PlanStore loaded from .vrooli/plans.json.

Swarm Manager stats and overview endpoints are unauthenticated (fail-open identity middleware on port 8080). Stats uses an event-sourced watermark pattern — incremental aggregation from SQLite event log, held in memory. Overview does a full load per request (all backlog items + initiatives + dependency graph). Both return rich, well-structured JSON that command-center can consume directly with minimal transformation.

Vrooli Core API (port 8092) is unauthenticated and returns scenario listing with health_status, runtime, ports, and system_warnings. Completeness scoring is a SEPARATE scenario (scenario-completeness-scoring) with its own API — it exposes GET /api/v1/scores and GET /api/v1/scores/{scenario}/calculate. Command-center would need to call two different services for full scenario data.

LPBS price mapping: plans.json defines 8 price entries (4 tiers × 2 intervals). Monthly amounts: solo=$29, pro=$79, studio=$199, business=$499. Yearly: solo=$239, pro=$648, studio=$1668, business=$4188. MRR calculation: for monthly subs use amount_cents directly; for yearly divide by 12. Filter subscriptions by status IN (active, trialing). Join subscriptions.price_id → plans.json via PlanStore.GetPlanByPriceID().

items.context: LPBS already has several admin API endpoints returning aggregated data (metrics/summary, admin/usage, admin/users, admin/coupons/usage), but is missing revenue/MRR and subscription-distribution endpoints. Two approaches: (A) use existing LPBS APIs where possible and add new summary endpoints to LPBS for missing data, or (B) connect command-center directly to LPBS Postgres for all queries.

options.label: API-first: use existing LPBS endpoints + add new summary endpoints to LPBS for missing aggregations (MRR, churn, subscription distribution)
options.rationale: Loose coupling — LPBS owns its data contracts. Command-center only depends on stable API surface. Avoids schema coupling. Requires coordinated work on LPBS to add ~3 new endpoints.

options.label: Direct DB: command-center connects to LPBS Postgres for all queries
options.rationale: Maximum flexibility — can compute any aggregation. No LPBS code changes. But tightly couples command-center to LPBS schema, risks breaking on migrations, and violates the read-only-view-layer principle.

options.label: Hybrid: use existing LPBS APIs where they exist, direct DB only for the specific aggregations not yet exposed
options.rationale: Pragmatic middle ground — minimizes new LPBS endpoints while limiting schema coupling to a few well-defined queries. Adds operational complexity of maintaining two connection types.

items.topic: Where to compute derived metrics (MRR, churn rate, ARPU)
items.context: Derived metrics like MRR require joining subscriptions with price data (plans.json). Churn rate needs canceled_at timestamps over time windows. ARPU divides revenue by active subscribers. These can be computed either by LPBS (new endpoints) or by command-center (from raw data).

options.label: LPBS computes derived metrics and exposes them via new admin endpoints
options.rationale: Single source of truth for business metric definitions. Other consumers (CLI, reports) get the same numbers. But requires LPBS code changes for every new metric.

options.label: Command-center computes derived metrics from raw LPBS data
options.rationale: Command-center is self-contained — no LPBS changes needed. But risks metric definition drift if another consumer calculates differently.

items.context: Command-center queries 3+ upstream sources. Need to define TTLs and behavior when a source is down.

options.label: In-memory TTL cache per source (30s LPBS, 30s Swarm Manager, 60s Vrooli Core), serve stale on failure with staleness timestamp
options.rationale: Simple, fast, no external dependency. Stale data is better than error screens for a dashboard. Different TTLs match source update frequency.

options.label: Redis-backed cache with configurable TTLs per endpoint
options.rationale: Survives API restarts, shareable across instances. But adds infrastructure dependency for a single-instance service.

items.text: Gap metadata recommendation: The gap tracking system should be API-side, not UI-side. Each metric in the API response should include a 'source' field (live/gap/partial). The static registry lives in command-center's Go code (a map of metric-name → source-status). GET /api/v1/gaps returns the full registry filtered to gap/partial entries. When a data pipeline is built, the registry entry flips to 'live' — this is a code change, not a runtime config change. This aligns with the orchestration summary's feedback loop design.
